articles.title: Rubio spoke with Lebanon's Aoun about confiscation of explosives from Hezbollah, US official says
articles.body:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun about the confiscation of hundreds of kilograms of explosives from Hezbollah, a US State Department official said on Thursday.
Rubio urged Aoun to hold accountable those who ordered, financed and directed the shipment, and "underscored that returning explosives to (Hezbollah) should be out of the question," the US official said.
Rubio urged direct military-to-military communication between Lebanese and Israeli forces "for deconfliction," the official added.
A Hezbollah lawmaker said earlier the explosives seized last week by Lebanese security forces belonged to his group.
The lawmaker, Hassan Fadlallah, said Hezbollah had intended to use the explosives against Israel, whose troops are occupying swathes of Lebanese territory seized in this year's war.
A Hezbollah official and a Lebanese security source told Reuters the explosives seized in a car last week were intended to be used in explosive drones targeting Israeli troops.
Aoun told Rubio the Lebanese army and security forces were fully carrying out decisions to prevent armed displays, confiscate weapons and combat smuggling, the presidency said, adding Aoun asked Rubio to pressure Israel to halt attacks on southern Lebanese towns and villages.
Hezbollah military activities banned by Lebanese government
On March 2, the Lebanese government specifically banned Hezbollah's military activities after the movement launched rockets at Israel to back up Tehran, pulling Lebanon into the broader US-Israeli war on Iran that began on February 28.
Tehran subsequently launched its own strikes on Israel and Gulf states that host US bases. US-Israeli strikes on Iran and Israeli attacks on Lebanon during the war have killed thousands and displaced millions.
Under a deal reached through US-brokered Israel-Lebanon talks, Beirut vowed to disarm Hezbollah, which would in turn lead to Israeli troops gradually withdrawing from Lebanon. But Hezbollah has refused to disarm as long as Israeli forces remain on Lebanese land and Israel has continued striking southern Lebanon.

Ukrainian specialists also shared combat experience with NATO partners, including lessons from the use of unmanned systems in maritime operations.

articles.title: Ukraine: Critical health supplies destroyed in ongoing Russian attacks
articles.body:
Ukraine: Critical health supplies destroyed in ongoing Russian attacks
Ongoing and deadly Russian attacks across Ukraine are causing serious healthcare disruption, with more than $1.5 million-worth of medicines and supplies destroyed in four separate strikes on warehouses used by the UN there since July.
According to the World Health Organization (WHO), 21 warehouses have been targeted this year, out of a total of 400 incidents, almost all involving heavy weapons which is classified as firearms, tanks, missiles, bombs and mortars.
Speaking to UN News, WHO Communications Officer Sarah Tyler described what WHO witnessed at hospitals and warehouses that had come under attack: “When you stand in those places, you really understand what the numbers mean.
“In just three months, four warehouses used by WHO were hit and three were destroyed…The health workers I met keep caring for patients under extraordinary pressure; protecting health care means protecting them.”
Growing toll
The development comes amid a large wave of large-scale attacks by Russian forces across Ukraine this week. Strikes overnight into Wednesday killed at least three people in Kyiv and left hundreds of thousands without power.
This was despite the announcement by President Trump last Friday of an “energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine.
Over the weekend, other Russian attacks included one in Zaporizhzhia that killed more than 20 people including four children.
Following the bombing, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) highlighted the “unimaginable loss” for families, insisting that the violence “must not become the new normal”.
WHO has verified more than 3,300 attacks on healthcare since the full-scale Russian invasion in February 2022. A total of 247 people have been killed and more than 1,090 health workers and patients have been injured, according to data compiled by the agency.
The agency underlined that the consequences of attacks extend well beyond damage to individual buildings. “When warehouses and other humanitarian installations are hit, medicines, medical equipment, laboratory reagents and other essential supplies can be lost, disrupting the support that health facilities need to treat patients,” explained Dr Ihor Perehinets, WHO Regional Emergency and Health Security Director.
Under pressure
He stressed that Ukraine’s health workers face “extraordinary pressure” while continuing to deliver care.
“Protecting health services means protecting the people who provide them, as well as the medical supplies, equipment and humanitarian infrastructure on which their work depends,” Dr Perehinets added.
The agency’s support in Ukraine includes emergency response, assistance with trauma care, medical supply provision, energy resilience and developing the capacity to manage chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear incidents.
WHO’s 2026 Ukraine appeal seeks $42 million to support 700,000 people.
Continued funding is important to sustaining emergency health operations, maintaining access to essential services, replenishing medical supplies and strengthening preparedness.

A horrific Russian strike with a jet-powered "Shahed" drone on an ordinary store in Odesa region. Russia continues its bloody terror. The store was partially destroyed, and cars were damaged. The President stressed: "It is important that our partners help protect against this." "Residential buildings, stores, the energy sector, and other critical infrastructure are effectively under attack constantly. Not a single hour of calm," Zelenskyy said.
"What is happening is Russia's demonstrative response to the signals it is receiving from America. Unfortunately, these are dangerous signals regarding the possible further lifting of sanctions. articles.body:
Ukrainian drones reportedly strike Yandex data center, warehouses in overnight attack on Russia
Editor's Note: This is a developing story and is being updated.
Ukrainian forces appeared to strike multiple targets across Russia's Moscow, Rostov, and Vladimir regions in a widespread drone attack overnight on Oct. 16.
The Kyiv Independent can not independently verify attack targets or damage at this time.
According to monitoring channels ExileNova+ and SuperNova+, Russian technology giant Yandex's data center in Vladimir Oblast, around 500 kilometers (310 miles) from the Ukrainian border, was targeted in the overnight operation.
Footage from residents at the scene shows large explosions and air defense systems operating around residential buildings.
Following strikes on the same Yandex site on Oct. 11, the company announced operations at the data center had been completely shut down. That strike marked the third near-consecutive day of attacks on Yandex data centers in Russia, following confirmed strikes in Ryazan and Kaluga oblasts on Oct. 8 and 9.
The string of attacks on Russian data centers follows President Volodymyr Zelensky's statement that Ukraine would retaliate in kind to Russian strikes on Ukrainian internet infrastructure.
Earlier in the night around Moscow, Ukrainian drones shut down airspace above multiple airports. According to Russian opposition news channel Astra, plane departures and arrivals to the Vnukovo, Domodedovo, Zhukovsky, and Sheremetyevo airports were canceled overnight.
Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said that over 59 Ukrainian drones were destroyed by the capital's air defense system throughout the night.
The closure of Moscow's airspace partially realizes threats made by Zelensky in September when he promised that Russian skies would soon be "de facto closed."
"There will simply be drones in Russia's skies on a scale that has to be taken into account," said Zelensky.
It is currently unclear what, if any, targets were hit around Moscow. Eyewitness footage from city residents shows what appears to be flames illuminating the night sky, accompanied by the sounds of drones overhead and loud explosions.
Previously, several Moscow airports temporarily suspended flights on Oct. 9, as suspected Ukrainian drones and balloons entered airspace around the Russian capital.
Over 950 kilometers (590 miles) southeast of Moscow, Ukrainian drones attacked targets in the Rostov Oblast.
According to regional Governor Yuri Slusar, production and storage facilities were damaged, and a fire broke out as a result of the drone attack in the town of Aksay. The Chertkovsky district and the city of Bataysk in the region were also targeted, Slusar said.

Zelenskyy says Poland has provided Ukraine with aid to defend Kyiv

Details: Welcoming the Ukrainian president, Tusk emphasised that Ukraine can count on Polish assistance.

This is exactly what we are now asking various countries, and all of Europe, for," Zelenskyy stated.

A night under Russian strikes: which regions of Ukraine did the enemy attack and what is known about the consequences
Kyiv • UNN
During the night of October 15, the Russians attacked Ukraine with missiles and drones. At least 5 people were killed and 7 more were injured.
Russian forces attacked several regions of Ukraine with missiles and drones during the night of October 15. At least 5 people are known to have been killed and 7 wounded; residential buildings and industrial enterprises were damaged. The heads of regional military administrations reported the consequences of the shelling, UNN writes.
Details
In the Dnipropetrovsk region, the Russians launched strikes on the Dnipro and Pavlohrad districts early in the morning. Strikes on Zaporizhzhia, the Poltava region and Odesa
In the Zaporizhzhia region, 7 people were wounded as a result of Russian shelling of the regional capital and the Zaporizhzhia district. According to Ivan Fedorov, head of the regional military administration, over the past day the occupiers launched 964 strikes on 61 settlements in the region.
In particular, Russian forces launched 2 missile strikes on Zaporizhzhia and carried out 25 airstrikes on settlements in the region, including Vilniansk, Kushuhum, Balabyne, Veselianka, Zarichne, Preobrazhenka and others.
